title: Impact of Obesity Diagnosis on Medication Use

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Causal method: Sharp Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD)

Rationale  
• Treatment (receiving an obesity diagnosis) turns on mechanically when BMI crosses a fixed medical cutoff.  
• BMI is a continuously measured “running variable”; individuals just above and below the threshold are assumed comparable.  
• Therefore, the discontinuity in the outcome (log medication use) at the cutoff identifies the causal effect of the diagnosis.

Key assumptions  
1. Continuity: In the absence of the diagnosis, expected log medication use is continuous in BMI at the cutoff (no other factor jumps exactly there).  
2. No precise manipulation: Individuals cannot perfectly sort their BMI to just below or above the threshold.  
3. Local randomization: Within a narrow bandwidth around the cutoff, treated and control units are as-if randomly assigned.  

## 2. R Code
```r
############################################
# Impact of Obesity Diagnosis on Medication
# Sharp RDD at the BMI cutoff
############################################

# 0. Packages --------------------------------------------------------------
need <- c("tidyverse","rdrobust","rddensity")
inst  <- need[!need %in% installed.packages()[,"Package"]]
if(length(inst)) install.packages(inst, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
library(tidyverse)
library(rdrobust)
library(rddensity)

# 1. Read data -------------------------------------------------------------
df <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s100_data.csv",
               col_types = cols())

# 2. Set cutoff ------------------------------------------------------------
c_star <- 0.5           # visual inspection shows treatment = 1 if BMI ≥ 0.5

# 3. Main RD estimate ------------------------------------------------------
rd_main <- rdrobust(y = df$y,
                    x = df$running_var,
                    c = c_star,              # cutoff
                    p = 1)                   # local linear (default)

cat("\n=== Main RD Estimate (local treatment effect) ===\n")
print(rd_main$coef[1])                       # point estimate
cat("Robust SE:", rd_main$se[1], "\n")
cat("95% CI: [", rd_main$ci[1,1], ",", rd_main$ci[1,2], "]\n")

# 4. McCrary density test (manipulation check) ----------------------------
dens <- rddensity(X = df$running_var, c = c_star)
cat("\n=== McCrary Density Test ===\n")
print(dens$test)

# 5. Robustness checks -----------------------------------------------------

# 5a. Different bandwidth (use half the MSE-optimal bandwidth)
h_small <- rd_main$bws[1,1] / 2
rd_small <- rdrobust(y = df$y,
                     x = df$running_var,
                     c = c_star,
                     h = h_small, p = 1)

cat("\nRD with half-bandwidth (h =", round(h_small,3), "):\n")
print(rd_small$coef[1])

# 5b. Higher-order polynomial (quadratic)
rd_quad <- rdrobust(y = df$y,
                    x = df$running_var,
                    c = c_star,
                    p = 2)

cat("\nRD with quadratic fit (p = 2):\n")
print(rd_quad$coef[1])

# 5c. Placebo cutoff 0.4 (should be ~0)
placebo_cut <- 0.4
rd_placebo <- rdrobust(y = df$y,
                       x = df$running_var,
                       c = placebo_cut,
                       p = 1)

cat("\nPlacebo cutoff at 0.4 (expect no jump):\n")
print(rd_placebo$coef[1])
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Sign: Positive – being labeled obese should raise medication use because physicians initiate pharmacological treatment for weight-related comorbidities (hypertension, diabetes, etc.) once a formal diagnosis is recorded.

Magnitude: Roughly +0.25 – 0.35 in log points (≈ 28-42 % increase). The jump is expected to be economically meaningful but not huge, reflecting that only some newly diagnosed patients receive additional drugs immediately after the diagnostic threshold.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare medication use for individuals just above and below the BMI cutoff.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Receiving an obesity diagnosis at the BMI cutoff leads to increased medication use.
